FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Animals & Their Habitats flashcards.

Twenty-two cards that answer a very big question in a very small way: where do animals live? A rabbit in the meadow, a frog on the pond, a koala in the eucalyptus tree, a camel between the dunes, a whale under the waves and a bat hanging in the cave — every card one animal in the home that fits it, ready to sort, match and talk about.

These cards belong to Class 36 · Animals & Their Habitats on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Sort the cards by home

    Deal the cards out and make piles: who lives in the grass, who in the water, who in the trees, who in the cold? Six habitat piles later, the whole set has been read twice.

  2. 02

    Play the matching question

    Hold up a card and ask "could the whale live in the desert?" Silly matches make children shout the right answer — and shouting the right answer means knowing it.

  3. 03

    Find each home on a map or a walk

    The meadow and the pond might be down the street; the savanna and the arctic live on the globe. Big words land when small feet and paper maps hold them.

  4. 04

    Act out each animal at home

    Hop like the kangaroo on the grassland, waddle like the penguin on the ice, swing your arms like the monkey in the trees. Bodies remember habitats better than lists do.

      Rabbit Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A soft beige rabbit sits on a green mound — a meadow is a rabbit’s dining room and its hiding place at once.

      How the card helps

      Opens the habitat question with an animal children already know from storybooks.

      A habitat game

      Crouch low on a lawn and pretend the grass towers overhead — meadow height, not people height.

      What it teaches

      Every animal needs food and shelter, and the meadow hands the rabbit both at once.

      Print it like this

      Low on the nature wall, at sitting-eye level for floor play.

      One more idea

      Ask "could the rabbit live in our street?" — then find the grass patch that says maybe.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Rabbit lesson on the Learning Path.

      Frog Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A smiling green frog sits on a lily pad between the reeds — a pond gives a frog water to swim, food to catch and a place to raise tadpoles.

      How the card helps

      Turns the pond from scenery into a frog-sized house with water wings included.

      A habitat game

      Sit cross-legged as a lily pad, then "plop!" sideways into an imaginary pond at the first loud noise.

      What it teaches

      Some homes are half water — and pond animals are built for exactly that half.

      Print it like this

      Bathroom door — the one room where a pond joke lands daily.

      One more idea

      Hum one croak note and let your child match the pitch; frog voices are elastic bands.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Frog lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Squirrel Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A red-brown squirrel holds an acorn in both paws — woodland gives the squirrel trees to climb and a pantry to fill for winter.

      How the card helps

      Shows a habitat doing double duty as a pantry that has to last all winter.

      A habitat game

      Hide five acorns, be the squirrel, gather them fast — then test the memory a real squirrel needs.

      What it teaches

      Woodland animals store food in autumn because the trees stop giving in winter.

      Print it like this

      Beside the autumn craft shelf, where the leaves and pinecones live.

      One more idea

      Wonder aloud where the forgotten acorns end up — new trees is the answer worth waiting for.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Squirrel lesson on the Learning Path.

      Fox Flashcard for Preschoolers

      An orange fox sits calmly between the pines and bushes — woodland edges, thickets and quiet corners are a fox’s favourite streets.

      How the card helps

      Introduces the quiet night-shift side of the woodland most children never see.

      A habitat game

      Tiptoe a silent fox-path between the furniture — soft paws only, no bumps allowed.

      What it teaches

      Some animals sleep by day and roam by night, using the same home at a different hour.

      Print it like this

      Bedroom door — out with the fox, in with the dreams.

      One more idea

      On a dusk walk, whisper "fox hour" — the quiet between dog-walks is when foxes commute.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Fox lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Owl Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A brown owl with big golden eyes perches on a branch high above the pines — the forest floor below is an owl’s hunting table.

      How the card helps

      Puts the forest in a vertical light: the owl’s home is a branch with a view of everything below.

      A habitat game

      Stand on the "branch" (a cushion), swivel your head slowly like an owl scanning, then swoop on a toy mouse.

      What it teaches

      Forests stack homes in layers — up high, eye level and underfoot all house somebody.

      Print it like this

      High on the wall — owls belong at ceiling height, looking down.

      One more idea

      Test silent flight: flap a tea towel slowly; fast flaps whoosh, owl feathers are built for hush.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Owl lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Koala Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A grey koala hugs a eucalyptus branch — almost everything a koala needs, food included, grows on one kind of tree.

      How the card helps

      Nails the specialist idea: one animal, one tree, one very picky dinner.

      A habitat game

      Koala-hug a doorframe for a slow ten — grip like you mean it, then slide down boneless like a sleepy koala.

      What it teaches

      Some animals can only live where their one food grows — the tree is the address.

      Print it like this

      Kitchen wall, right by the "what we eat" talk — koalas have opinions too.

      One more idea

      Ask what your child would eat if only ONE food existed — then reveal the koala actually lives that choice.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Koala lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Panda Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A black-and-white panda ambles between tall bamboo stalks — a cool, misty forest that is also the panda’s one and only cafeteria.

      How the card helps

      Makes a cool misty mountain forest feel real through a hungry, cheerful resident.

      A habitat game

      Hold a breadstick in both paws and munch sideways like a panda working through a bamboo stalk.

      What it teaches

      Habitats feed their animals — and the panda picked the crunchiest menu in the forest.

      Print it like this

      Snack shelf, guarding the crackers at panda eye level.

      One more idea

      Pandas eat for hours a day. Time one snack slowly — "how long would bamboo breakfast take?"

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Panda lesson on the Learning Path.

      Monkey Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A smiling brown monkey sits deep in the green — the rainforest canopy is a monkey’s highway, playground and fruit shop in one.

      How the card helps

      Explains the treetop life where the ground is nobody’s address and branches are roads.

      A habitat game

      Cross the climbing frame or sofa-back hand-over-hand — the floor is lava, canopy rules only.

      What it teaches

      Rainforests crowd life upward: most rainforest animals live their whole lives in the trees.

      Print it like this

      Playroom, right beside the climbing corner it belongs to.

      One more idea

      Monkeys live in troops — assign family roles for one round of play and hear the chattering start.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Monkey lesson on the Learning Path.

      Zebra Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A striped zebra stands among tall green blades — the grassland is an open dining hall, and the stripes are the zebra’s own dazzle trick.

      How the card helps

      Uses the boldest pattern in nature to show how open-country animals stay safe.

      A habitat game

      Wave a striped sock while jogging in a circle — count how quickly eyes lose track of the edges.

      What it teaches

      Stripes blur a moving zebra into a dazzle; big open homes demand clever tricks.

      Print it like this

      Playroom wall where things move fast — the stripes suit the spot.

      One more idea

      No two zebras share stripes. Ask how your child would tell twin zebras apart — then check fingerprints.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Zebra lesson on the Learning Path.

      Kangaroo Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A tan kangaroo stands tall between grass tussocks — big hind legs built for bouncing across the open plains.

      How the card helps

      Delivers the wide-open-plains idea through the animal that bounces across them.

      A habitat game

      Hop a kangaroo race — feet glued together, hands as paws, no walking steps allowed.

      What it teaches

      Open grasslands suit big movers: speed and bounce replace walls and corners.

      Print it like this

      Hallway floor tip — taped at hop-distance markers, ten hops wide.

      One more idea

      Kangaroos cannot walk backwards. Try it — the stiff hop is a real physics lesson.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Kangaroo lesson on the Learning Path.

      Elephant Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A grey elephant stands in golden grass under an acacia tree — the savanna’s biggest resident is also its keenest gardener.

      How the card helps

      Shows an animal big enough to reshape its own habitat — and generous with it.

      A habitat game

      Dig a one-arm "water hole" in the sandpit, trumpet proudly, then let every toy animal drink from it.

      What it teaches

      Some habitats are shaped by their residents — elephant paths and pools serve everyone.

      Print it like this

      Living room low shelf, beside the toy animals that will queue at the water hole.

      One more idea

      Say "savanna" with a long open AHH — the word sounds like the wide space it names.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Elephant lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Lion Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A golden lion with a great dark mane sits on warm sand — most of savanna life, for a lion, is a very good nap in the shade.

      How the card helps

      Upsides the fierce-lion story: most savanna hours belong to the nap in the shade.

      A habitat game

      Pride nap for a slow twenty, then one silent prowl around the room — prowl first, nap is earned after.

      What it teaches

      Resting is part of the job: lions save energy for the cool hours, and shade is furniture.

      Print it like this

      Beside the bed — the good-nap card, for pride-level napping.

      One more idea

      Tawny coat, dry grass — ask what colour a lion would need in snow, and let the mismatch land.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Lion lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Camel Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A tan camel stands between rolling dunes — the desert’s heat, sand and long empty miles are exactly what a camel is built for.

      How the card helps

      Corrects the classic hump mix-up early: fat for the journey, not a water tank.

      A habitat game

      Heel-to-toe across the cushion dunes — wide steady feet, arms out, no soft-sand stumbles.

      What it teaches

      Desert animals carry their own supplies and wear the desert on their bodies.

      Print it like this

      By the shoe rack — camel feet before outdoor shoes, all-terrain talk.

      One more idea

      Long lashes, shut nostrils, kneeling knees — tick each camel feature off on the card like equipment.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Camel lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Beaver Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A brown beaver with a paddle tail sits on its riverbank — and with those teeth it does not just live in the river, it rebuilds it.

      How the card helps

      Introduces the one animal that builds its habitat instead of just moving in.

      A habitat game

      Dam the bath or a garden trickle with twigs and watch the water pool behind your engineering.

      What it teaches

      Beavers change rivers into ponds — and the pond becomes home for many more animals.

      Print it like this

      By the bath toys — the dam experiment is a nightly possibility now.

      One more idea

      Flat tail as a rudder, teeth as an axe, waterproof coat — go through the beaver toolkit slowly.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Beaver lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Turtle Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A green sea turtle rests where the wave meets the sand — the coast is a two-home address: beach above, sea below.

      How the card helps

      Splits one life across two homes — sandy beach above, open sea below.

      A habitat game

      One side of the room is sea, one is beach — call the turtle actions and dash between homes.

      What it teaches

      Some animals hold two addresses, and the coast is where both meet.

      Print it like this

      By the bath or beach-bag hook — the two-home card goes where swimming lives.

      One more idea

      Baby turtles sprint to the sea the night they hatch — act the dash; it is the best race in nature.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Turtle lesson on the Learning Path.

      Fish Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A smiling blue fish glides over the sandy seabed — the ocean is the world’s biggest home, and fish are the family that never leaves it.

      How the card helps

      States the biggest fact in the set: the ocean is the largest habitat on the planet.

      A habitat game

      Fish-mouth breathing contest — open and close, gills working, no air allowed in the pretend.

      What it teaches

      Fish breathe water through gills; we breathe air — the swap is impossible both ways.

      Print it like this

      Playroom, at swimming-toy height, where the ocean already lives.

      One more idea

      Globe check: spin it and see the blue win — that is why this card says biggest.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Fish lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Dolphin Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A grey dolphin leaps above the waves — a dolphin lives in the ocean but breathes air like us, so it keeps coming up to say hello.

      How the card helps

      Adds the twist that ocean animals still need air — the leap is a breath, not a stunt.

      A habitat game

      Carpet-swim, then "surface" with a huge proud breath every few strokes — dolphin lung rules.

      What it teaches

      Dolphins breathe air like us and talk in whistles — the ocean home with lungs.

      Print it like this

      Bedroom wall, high like a leaping dolphin, mid-jump over the bed.

      One more idea

      Invent a family whistle for each of you — dolphins name themselves in sound; try it at bath time.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Dolphin lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Whale Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A great blue whale glides over the waves — the largest animal that has ever lived makes its home in the largest home there is.

      How the card helps

      Carries the set’s biggest wow: the largest animal ever lives in the largest home there is.

      A habitat game

      Pace out a whale on the floor in heel-to-toe steps — the whole family fits inside one, nose to tail.

      What it teaches

      The ocean can hold animals bigger than any that ever walked the land.

      Print it like this

      Hallway wall, long-ways — the only card that needs the length of a corridor.

      One more idea

      Biggest eater, tiniest food: whales strain seas of tiny creatures — big and gentle can share a body.

      Teach it, step by step

      Penguin Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A black-and-white penguin stands on an ice floe — in the polar region even the ground is white, and the water below is the cold larder.

      How the card helps

      Makes the frozen world friendly through its best-dressed, waddliest resident.

      A habitat game

      Waddle across the room, then belly-slide the last stretch onto a cushion ice floe — penguin commute done right.

      What it teaches

      Polar homes are white, the water below is the supermarket, and huddles keep everyone warm.

      Print it like this

      By the coat hooks — a waddle is mandatory on the way to winter clothes.

      One more idea

      Huddle game: whole family in one small circle, taking turns on the "cold outside edge" — fairness keeps penguins warm.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Penguin lesson on the Learning Path.

      Seal Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A grey spotted seal rests on an ice floe under the snowy hills — half its life on the ice, half in the water, both polar.

      How the card helps

      Shows the half-and-half polar life: flopped out on ice, hunting below it.

      A habitat game

      Seal scoot: push up on hands and toes and flop forward three times — harder than seals make it look.

      What it teaches

      Blubber is a built-in coat; ice is both bedroom and diving platform.

      Print it like this

      Beside the penguin card — the polar neighbours belong side by side.

      One more idea

      Whisker test: eyes closed, find what a gentle fingertip can sense — seals feel fish with theirs in the dark.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Seal lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Polar Bear Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A creamy-white polar bear stands on sea ice — to the biggest bear in the world, the frozen ocean is home, hunting ground and highway.

      How the card helps

      Delivers camouflage in its purest form: white on white, and the hunt depends on it.

      A habitat game

      Hold a white paper bear against the white wall, then against the colourful poster — see it vanish, then reappear.

      What it teaches

      The arctic’s biggest hunter wears its habitat — and the sea ice is its kitchen floor.

      Print it like this

      Fridge door — white bear, white fridge, instant camouflage joke at breakfast.

      One more idea

      Polar bears wait still as statues at breathing holes — one patient stand-up freeze teaches what that waiting costs.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Polar Bear lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Animals & Their Habitats (Class 36) class on the Learning Path.

      Bat Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A smiling grey bat hangs upside down inside a rocky cave — the cave is dark, quiet and exactly right for sleeping the day away.

      How the card helps

      Ends the set with the strangest address: a bedroom where everyone sleeps upside down.

      A habitat game

      Bat-hang over a grown-up’s arm, head low, flap twice, then "fly" out of the cave for the night shift.

      What it teaches

      Caves are dark, still and safe — exactly what a daytime sleeper needs most.

      Print it like this

      Inside a wardrobe door — open it, and that is the cave with the card in it.

      One more idea

      Clap in the hallway and catch the echo — bats read rooms with sound, and that clap is a tiny taste of it.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bat lesson on the Learning Path.
